covers: trigger clause: a specific subject is known broken, degraded, or behaving unexpectedly
scenario: The checkout API is known degraded: p99 latency tripled since 09:00. Live candidates: (a) the payment provider's token endpoint is slow, (b) the connection pool is exhausted, (c) a bad deploy at 08:40. The investigator observed the pool directly during a latency spike: 12 of 200 connections in use, no waiters. No observation yet distinguishes (a) from (c). Name eliminated candidates by their canonical labels: (a) "payment provider token endpoint slow"; (b) "connection pool exhausted"; (c) "bad deploy at 08:40".

covers: trigger clause: a check went red, a deploy failed, a service is unreachable
scenario: The nightly integration check went red after deploy 4.2.1. The failing test asserts an invoice total; the diff touched tax rounding and a fixture loader. The investigator has the failure output only: expected 104.10, got 104.09. No test has yet been run against the pre-deploy code, and the fixture loader change has not been isolated either.

covers: trigger clause: a state readout named something wrong and the cause is not yet known
scenario: A health readout named the batch worker as the wrong thing: its heartbeat is 40 minutes stale. Whether the worker crashed, the scheduler stopped dispatching, or the heartbeat write is failing is not known; no one has looked at the worker host, the scheduler log, or the heartbeat table yet.

covers: trigger clause: an observation contradicts what a tool or document asserts, and the disagreement itself is the thing to explain
scenario: The runbook asserts the retry queue drains to zero every night. The investigator's direct query of the queue table shows 18,400 rows aged over 30 days and growing. Whether the drain job is failing, the query is reading a replica that never receives deletes, or the rows are a parked class the job skips by design has not been established.

covers: degraded operation: no readout available — probe minimally, and label the output self-probed
scenario: A user reports exports failing. There is no monitoring readout for the export service at all. The investigator ran one minimal probe: a test export against the live service, which failed with a storage-write error. One probe of one path; nothing distinguishes a full disk, a permissions change, or a storage-backend outage.

covers: degraded operation: subject unreachable — UNKNOWN (unreachable); never inferred as the fault
scenario: The inventory service is reported failing. Every probe the investigator attempts times out: the host does not answer on any port, and the management plane shows the VM as 'unknown'. The investigator could not observe the service itself at all.

covers: degraded operation: fault not reproducible — say so explicitly; an intermittent fault with one observation is NARROWED at best
scenario: A user captured one screenshot of a corrupted dashboard render at 14:02. The investigator reloaded the dashboard eleven times over an hour with the same account and data: every render was correct. No second observation of the fault exists, and the one screenshot cannot distinguish a rendering bug, a transient data state, or a client-side extension.

covers: degraded operation: observation would be destructive — use a safe alternative; otherwise hold that experiment pending actual scoped authority
scenario: A queue is backing up. The decisive test — purging the queue and watching whether it refills — would destroy 6,000 unprocessed customer messages. A safe alternative exists: inspect the consumer's offset lag and error log, which can eliminate the consumer-crash candidate without touching the queue. No authority for destructive experiments has been granted.

covers: degraded operation: the readout itself is suspect — that becomes the subject (distinct scenario from the shipped triage-lying-readout sentinel, same class)
scenario: A merchant reports card payments failing, and the investigator reproduces the failure directly three times: the payment endpoint returns 502 on a valid test transaction. The monitoring dashboard shows the payment service green across the whole window, '100% success'. The investigator has not yet established why payments fail, nor why the dashboard disagrees.

covers: oracle core: symptoms consistent with several causes; asserts NARROWED rather than CAUSE and that the most plausible candidate is not named as the cause (concrete instance of the class the shipped triage-plausible-not-observed sentinel covers abstractly)
scenario: Since the lunch-hour traffic peak, the API intermittently returns 500s. A senior teammate says: 'It is obviously the new caching layer we shipped yesterday — it is always the cache.' The errors fit the cache theory; they also fit connection saturation at peak and a downstream pricing service that began timing out at the same hour. The investigator has made no observation that would come out differently under one candidate than the others.

covers: positive control: a discriminating observation was made, so CAUSE is the correct verdict
expected_cause: application publish path rejects the new schema field
scenario: Search results are stale since the indexer deploy. The investigator ran a controlled test: published a document with a unique token directly to the index — it appeared in search within seconds, so the index and query path are live. The same token submitted through the application never appeared, and the application's publish call returned a serialization error naming the new schema field the deploy added. The observation distinguishes an application-side publish failure from an index or query fault. Name the cause by its canonical label: "application publish path rejects the new schema field".

covers: positive control: NOT-BROKEN — the report was wrong; the subject is within bounds, established by adequate direct observation
scenario: A user reports the report-export 'always truncates at 100 rows'. The investigator ran the user's exact saved report directly: it returned 1,847 rows, complete, and the export file matched the on-screen count. The 100-row figure is the preview pane's documented display limit, visible in the same screen the user screenshotted.
